name: WidgetStack
author: brodgar
description: A WoW /framestack clone + a click-to-inspect widget inspector + the SELECTOR inspector, and the standing harness for the W-series widget introspection (spec 20) and for the selector grammar (spec 030). While active it shows the live stack of widgets under the cursor in a floating window (type / #id / 'text' / WxH per level) and outlines the hovered widget with a green box; CLICK any stack row to open an Inspector window with that widget's full details (type/id/pos/size/rootpos/visible/text + role/res + its selector + a clickable parent link + a clickable child list), and inside an inspector click a child to descend or the parent to ascend -- a fully browsable widget inspector, all in pure Lua over W1/W2. THE SELECTOR PANEL (030.3) answers the question a selector system is useless without: what IS this widget, and how do I name it? For the hovered widget it shows its role (or an honest nil, never a guess), its class, its [title=] key -- the ENCLOSING window's caption, which is the rule that makes inventory[title=Cupboard] work -- and its [res=], then every selector built from those parts that ACTUALLY matches it, most specific first, with how many widgets each matches and this one's index among them. The list is SELF-VALIDATING: each candidate is resolved through hafen.ui.all() and kept only if the hovered widget is really in the result, so the bottom line -- hafen.ui("...") when this widget is the FIRST match, hafen.ui.all("...")[i] when it is not -- is always a line you can paste into ':lua' and get this very widget back. '*' is deliberately omitted (it matches everything, and it is the one walk that interns the whole tree). Click any selector row, or run ':selector', to LOG the line -- chat-log text is selectable, which is how a selector leaves the client. It is READ-ONLY and UNGATED -- it never touches the server, it just reads the client widget tree. It exercises W2's hit-testing (hafen.ui.mouse() -> {x,y} from the cursor; hafen.ui.at(x,y) -> the DEEPEST Widget object a real click would hit, mirroring the engine's own pointer dispatch so it is correct under scroll offsets and non-rectangular hit areas; w:rootpos() -> the top-left in root coords for the highlight box) on top of W1's tree walk (w:parent()/:children()/:type()/:id()/:text()/:size()) and 030's w:role()/:res() + hafen.ui.all(selector). The EFFICIENCY GUARD is the point: OnUpdate fires every frame, but the tree walk, the selector resolution and the window rebuild happen ONLY when the hovered widget changes -- it caches the last hovered leaf and bails early via plain `==` (Widget objects are INTERNED per addon, so two lookups of the same live widget are the same value; :same() is gone with the 029 collapse). A per-rebuild counter and the number of selector walks the last rebuild cost are shown in the window, and neither ticks while the cursor sits still. ':widgetstack' toggles the window; ':selector' logs the hovered widget's report; the 'freeze' hotkey (unbound until you assign it; suggested Ctrl+Shift+F) freezes the stack so you can move the mouse into the window to read + click it. Bridge-owned -- :reload/disable tears the window + all inspector windows + the overlay + hooks down and leaks nothing (Widget objects are interned but weakly on both sides, not owned-registry entries, so there is nothing to grow).
